question: Which Chahamana ruler defeated Sultan Muhammad Ghori in 1191 A.D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prithviraja III.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Prithviraja III (पृथ्वीराज तृतीय), also known as Prithviraj Chauhan, was the Chahamana (Chauhan) ruler who defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain (1191 A.D.).

• The battle was fought near Tarain (Taraori) in present-day Haryana, and Ghori was wounded and forced to retreat.

• However, in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 A.D.), Muhammad Ghori defeated and captured Prithviraj Chauhan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Prithviraj Chauhan's court poet Chand Bardai wrote the epic 'Prithviraj Raso'.

• His capital was Ajmer, and he also controlled Delhi.

• The Second Battle of Tarain marked the beginning of Muslim rule in northern India.

NOTE

• Ajayaraja II (Option 1): An earlier Chahamana ruler credited with founding/developing the city of Ajmer.

• Vigraharaja IV (Option 2): A Chahamana king (Bisaldeo) who expanded the kingdom and captured Delhi; a patron of learning.

• Vigraharaja V (Option 4): A less prominent Chahamana ruler of the dynasty; not associated with the Tarain battles.

question: Which of the following is NOT a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
option_3: To value the rich heritage of our composite culture
solution_text:
The correct answer is To promote co-operative societies.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fundamental Duties (मौलिक कर्तव्य) are listed in Article 51A of Part IVA of the Indian Constitution.

• 'To promote co-operative societies' is NOT a Fundamental Duty; the promotion of co-operative societies is a Directive Principle of State Policy (Article 43B), inserted by the 97th Amendment, 2011.

• The other three options are genuine Fundamental Duties under Article 51A.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Originally there were 10 duties; the 86th Amendment (2002) added the 11th duty (right to education for children aged 6-14).

• Fundamental Duties are borrowed from the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

NOTE

• To protect integrity of India (Option 2): A genuine Fundamental Duty — to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India.

• To value the rich heritage of our composite culture (Option 3): A genuine Fundamental Duty under Article 51A.

• To develop the scientific temper (Option 4): A genuine Fundamental Duty — to develop scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

question: Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is NOT borrowed from Australia?
option_2: Joint sitting of the two houses
option_4: Election of members of the Rajya Sabha
solution_text:
The correct answer is Election of members of the Rajya Sabha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The election of members of the Rajya Sabha (राज्य सभा के सदस्यों का निर्वाचन) — election by an electoral college / indirect election method — is borrowed from the Constitution of South Africa (along with the amendment procedure), NOT from Australia.

• From Australia, India borrowed the Concurrent List, the joint sitting of the two Houses of Parliament, and freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• From the USA: Fundamental Rights, judicial review, independence of judiciary, impeachment of the President.

• From the UK: parliamentary government, rule of law, single citizenship, cabinet system.

• From Ireland: Directive Principles of State Policy, nomination of Rajya Sabha members, method of election of the President.

NOTE

• Concept of Concurrent list (Option 1): Borrowed from Australia.

• Joint sitting of the two houses (Option 2): Borrowed from Australia (Article 108).

• Freedom of trade and commerce (Option 3): Borrowed from Australia (Article 301).

question:
As of 31st July 2025, which of the following country is the member of BIMSTEC?
I. Thailand
II. Iran
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• BIMSTEC (बिम्सटेक) — Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation — has 7 member countries.

• Thailand is a founding member of BIMSTEC, while Iran is NOT a member. Hence only Statement I is correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• BIMSTEC members: Bangladesh, India, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Nepal and Bhutan.

• BIMSTEC was established on 6 June 1997 through the Bangkok Declaration.

• Its permanent Secretariat is in Dhaka, Bangladesh; the 6th BIMSTEC Summit was held in Bangkok in 2025.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect — Iran is not a BIMSTEC member.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect — Iran is not a member.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect — Thailand is a member.

question: The International Solar Alliance is a collaborative initiative between India and _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is France.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The International Solar Alliance (ISA) (अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सौर गठबंधन) is a joint initiative launched by India and France.

• It was launched by PM Narendra Modi and then French President Francois Hollande at the COP21 Paris Climate Summit in 2015.

• The ISA headquarters is at Gurugram, Haryana, India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• ISA is a treaty-based inter-governmental organisation of sun-rich countries lying fully or partially between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.

• Its main aim is 'One Sun, One World, One Grid' and to mobilise solar energy investment.

• The ISA Framework Agreement entered into force in December 2017.

NOTE

• USA (Option 2): A member/partner country but not the co-founder of ISA.

• Brazil (Option 3): Not a co-founder of the ISA.

• Italy (Option 4): Not associated with the founding of the ISA.

question: Who among the following is the first Indian woman mountaineer to climb Mount Everest?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bachendri Pal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bachendri Pal (बछेंद्री पाल) became the first Indian woman to summit Mount Everest on 23 May 1984.

• She was part of an Indian expedition and reached the 8,848 m summit, making history.

• She was born in Nakuri village, Uttarkashi (Uttarakhand).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• She was awarded the Padma Shri (1984), Padma Bhushan (2019) and the Arjuna Award.

• Junko Tabei of Japan was the first woman in the world to climb Everest (1975).

• Bachendri Pal later led adventure expeditions with the Tata Steel Adventure Foundation.

NOTE

• Ruma Pal (Option 1): A former judge of the Supreme Court of India, not a mountaineer.

• Cornelia Sorabji (Option 2): India's first woman lawyer and first woman to study law at Oxford.

• Shikha Sharma (Option 3 alt): A well-known Indian banker (former MD & CEO of Axis Bank), not a mountaineer.

question: Who was the first woman IPS officer of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kiran Bedi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kiran Bedi (किरण बेदी) became the first woman IPS (Indian Police Service) officer of India when she joined the service in 1972.

• She is renowned for her reforms as Inspector General of Tihar Jail, Delhi.

• She later served as the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry (2016–2021).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kiran Bedi received the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1994) for government service.

• She was also a national tennis champion in her youth.

• She was the first Indian and first woman to serve as a UN Police Advisor.

NOTE

• Annie Besant (Option 1): A social reformer and the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (1917).

• Matangini Hazra (Option 3): A freedom fighter ('Gandhi Buri') killed during the Quit India Movement in 1942.

• Lakshmi Sahgal (Option 4): A freedom fighter who led the Rani of Jhansi Regiment of the Indian National Army (INA).

question: In January 2025, who has been appointed as the India's new Ambassador to Israel?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jitender Pal Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jitender Pal Singh (जितेंद्र पाल सिंह), popularly known as JP Singh, was appointed India's new Ambassador to Israel in January 2025.

• He is a 1997-batch Indian Foreign Service (IFS) officer.

• Prior to this, he headed the Pakistan-Afghanistan-Iran (PAI) division in the Ministry of External Affairs.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• His appointment came at a critical time amid the West Asia / Israel-Gaza conflict.

• India and Israel share strong strategic, defence and agricultural cooperation ties.

• Diplomatic relations between India and Israel were established in 1992.

NOTE

• Amit Kumar (Option 1): Not the appointee for the Israel ambassadorship in this context.

• Akash Tripathi (Option 3): An IAS officer associated with Digital India / MyGov roles, not this posting.

• Ravi Ahuja (Option 4): Known as CEO of Sony Music Entertainment (global), not a diplomat.

question: In August 2024, which Indian received 'Grand-Collar of the Order' the highest civilian award of Timor Leste?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Droupadi Murmu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• President Droupadi Murmu (द्रौपदी मुर्मू) was conferred the 'Grand-Collar of the Order of Timor-Leste', the highest civilian award of Timor-Leste, in August 2024.

• It was conferred during her state visit to the capital Dili, marking the first-ever visit by an Indian President to Timor-Leste.

• The honour recognised her role in strengthening India–Timor-Leste bilateral relations.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Droupadi Murmu is the 15th President of India and the first tribal woman to hold the office.

• During the visit, both nations agreed to boost cooperation in trade, capacity building and development.

• She has received several international honours during her tenure as President.

NOTE

• Narendra Modi (Option 2): The Prime Minister of India; he has received many foreign honours but not this Timor-Leste award.

• Amit Shah (Option 3): The Union Home Minister of India, not the recipient.

• S. Jaishankar (Option 4): The Union Minister of External Affairs, not the recipient of this award.

question: In January 2025, The Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) of NITI Aayog launched _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is EmpowHER Biz – Sapno Ki Udaan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, the Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) (महिला उद्यमिता मंच) of NITI Aayog launched the 'EmpowHER Biz – Sapno Ki Udaan' programme.

• It aims to support and empower women entrepreneurs by providing them with mentoring, capacity building and market access.

• The initiative reflects NITI Aayog's push for women-led development ('Nari Shakti').

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Women Entrepreneurship Platform (WEP) was launched by NITI Aayog in 2018.

• WEP works to create an enabling ecosystem for women entrepreneurs across India.

• It was later transitioned into a public-private partnership mode.

NOTE

• Nari Shakti Puraskar (Option 1): India's highest civilian honour for women, given by the Ministry of Women and Child Development.

• Mahila Coir Yojana (Option 2): A scheme of the Coir Board to train and empower rural women artisans.

• SERB-POWER (Option 3): A scheme (Science and Engineering Research Board) to promote women in science and research.

question: In January 2025, what practice did the Supreme Court of India order to be completely stopped in six major metropolitan cities?
option_3: Manual scavenging and hazardous sewer cleaning
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manual scavenging and hazardous sewer cleaning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, the Supreme Court of India ordered that manual scavenging and hazardous sewer cleaning (मैनुअल स्कैवेंजिंग और खतरनाक सीवर सफाई) be completely stopped in six major metropolitan cities.

• The order targeted metros including Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru and Hyderabad.

• The Court directed authorities to file affidavits on the steps taken to end the practice.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Manual scavenging is banned under the Prohibition of Employment as Manual Scavengers and their Rehabilitation Act, 2013.

• The Supreme Court has repeatedly stressed the mechanisation of sewer cleaning to protect the dignity and lives of sanitation workers.

• Compensation of Rs 30 lakh for sewer deaths was earlier mandated in the Balram Singh (2023) judgment.

NOTE

• Open defecation (Option 1): Targeted under the Swachh Bharat Mission, not this specific SC order.

• Use of single use Plastic (Option 2): Banned by government notification (2022), not the subject of this order.

• Water rationing (Option 4): Not the subject of this Supreme Court directive.

question: Prime Minister's Internship Scheme (PMIS) aims to provide _____ crore young Indians with 12-month paid internships in the nation's top companies over the next five years.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Prime Minister's Internship Scheme (PMIS) (प्रधानमंत्री इंटर्नशिप योजना) aims to provide 1 crore young Indians with 12-month paid internships over five years.

• The internships are offered in the nation's top 500 companies.

• The scheme was announced in the Union Budget 2024-25.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Interns receive a monthly assistance of Rs 5,000 (Rs 4,500 from the government and Rs 500 from the company's CSR funds) plus a one-time grant of Rs 6,000.

• Eligible candidates are aged 21–24 years, not employed full-time and not enrolled full-time in education.

• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Corporate Affairs.

NOTE

• 2 (Option 2): Incorrect — the target is 1 crore, not 2 crore.

• 3 (Option 3): Incorrect figure for the PMIS internship target.

• 4 (Option 4): Incorrect figure for the PMIS internship target.

question: In July 2025, Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana has completed how many years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY) (प्रधानमंत्री कौशल विकास योजना) was launched on 15 July 2015.

• Therefore, in July 2025, it completed 10 years.

• 15 July is also observed as World Youth Skills Day.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• PMKVY is the flagship skill-development scheme of the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).

• It is implemented by the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).

• PMKVY 4.0 focuses on emerging technologies such as AI, robotics and drones.

NOTE

• 7 (Option 1): Incorrect — that would count from around 2018.

• 8 (Option 2): Incorrect — the scheme is older than 8 years in 2025.

• 9 (Option 3): Incorrect — 2015 to 2025 is a full 10 years.

question: A designated portion of a relay race is called as _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leg.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In athletics, a designated portion (segment) of a relay race (रिले दौड़) run by one team member is called a 'leg' (लेग).

• Each runner completes one leg and then passes the baton to the next runner.

• For example, in a 4x100 m relay each runner runs one 100 m leg.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The exchange of the baton must occur within a marked 'exchange/take-over zone'.

• Common relay events are the 4x100 m and 4x400 m relays.

• Dropping the baton or exchanging it outside the zone leads to disqualification.

NOTE

• Heat (Option 2): A preliminary/qualifying round of a race used to shortlist runners for the final.

• Spikes (Option 3): Special lightweight shoes with metal studs worn by track athletes for grip.

• Lifting (Option 4): Relates to weightlifting, not a segment of a relay race.

question: Long distance races are generally used to describe races of at least _____ metres.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Long distance races (लम्बी दूरी की दौड़) are generally used to describe track races of at least 3,000 metres.

• These include the 3000 m, 5000 m and 10,000 m events, along with road races like the marathon.

• Such races test an athlete's stamina and endurance.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Races up to 400 m are 'sprints'; 800 m and 1500 m are 'middle-distance' races.

• The marathon is 42.195 km long.

• The 3000 m steeplechase is a long-distance event with barriers and a water jump.

NOTE

• 1000 (Option 1): Falls in the middle-distance category, not long distance.

• 1500 (Option 2): The classic middle-distance 'metric mile' event.

• 15000 (Option 4): Not a standard threshold used to define long-distance track races.

question: India's first Vista dome jungle safari train was launched in which state in May 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's first Vista dome jungle safari train (विस्टा डोम जंगल सफारी ट्रेन) was launched in Uttar Pradesh in May 2025.

• The train runs through the forest region connecting Dudhwa and Katarniaghat wildlife areas.

• It features glass-roofed Vistadome coaches offering panoramic views of the jungle for eco-tourism.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The initiative promotes eco-tourism and wildlife tourism in the Terai region of UP.

• Vistadome coaches have large glass windows, a transparent roof and rotatable seats.

• Dudhwa Tiger Reserve is located in the Lakhimpur Kheri district of Uttar Pradesh.

NOTE

• Meghalaya (Option 1): Known for scenic railway/tourism but not the launch site of this train.

• Sikkim (Option 2): Did not host India's first Vistadome jungle safari train.

• Tripura (Option 4): Not associated with this jungle safari train launch.

question: As per the "Status of Tigers in Kaziranga, 2024" report what is the total number of tigers in Kaziranga Tiger reserve?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 148.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the 'Status of Tigers in Kaziranga, 2024' report, the total number of tigers in the Kaziranga Tiger Reserve (काजीरंगा टाइगर रिजर्व) is 148.

• This makes Kaziranga rank third globally in tiger density.

• The population showed a significant rise from the previous count.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kaziranga National Park is in Assam and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• It is famous for the largest population of the one-horned rhinoceros in the world.

• It lies on the banks of the Brahmaputra River.

NOTE

• 355 (Option 1): Not the figure reported for Kaziranga's tigers in the 2024 report.

• 68 (Option 2): An incorrect and lower figure, not matching the report.

• 252 (Option 4): An incorrect, inflated figure for Kaziranga's tiger count.

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of Indus Valley cities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Extensive use of iron tools.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Indus Valley Civilization (सिंधु घाटी सभ्यता) was a Bronze Age civilization; iron was NOT known to its people.

• Therefore, 'extensive use of iron tools' is NOT a feature of Indus Valley cities.

• The Harappans used tools and implements of copper and bronze.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Indus cities had a well-planned grid layout with roads cutting at right angles.

• They used standardised burnt bricks and had an advanced underground drainage system.

• Major sites include Harappa, Mohenjo-daro, Lothal, Dholavira and Kalibangan.

NOTE

• Roads intersecting at right angles (Option 1): A genuine feature — the grid pattern of town planning.

• Burnt brick construction (Option 3): A genuine feature — standardised kiln-fired bricks were used.

• Advanced drainage system (Option 4): A genuine feature — covered drains and soak pits along streets.

question: 'Nautanki' is a folk dance of which among the following state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nautanki (नौटंकी) is a popular folk theatre/dance form of Uttar Pradesh.

• It combines music, dance, drama and storytelling, and was a major form of rural entertainment before cinema.

• It is also popular in parts of northern India such as Rajasthan and Bihar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Uttar Pradesh include Raslila, Charkula, Kajri and Ramlila.

• The Kanpur, Hathras and Lucknow styles ('gharanas') of Nautanki are well known.

• Nautanki performances traditionally centred on legendary tales like 'Amar Singh Rathore' and 'Laila Majnu'.

NOTE

• Haryana (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Phag, Saang and Dhamal.

• Assam (Option 2): Known for the Bihu dance.

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for Lavani and Tamasha folk dance forms.

question: The 'Tapu' dance is traditionally performed by tribes belonging to which Indian state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arunachal Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Tapu dance (तपू नृत्य) is traditionally performed by the Adi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh.

• It is a war dance that depicts the valour and warrior spirit of the tribe.

• Dancers use war implements like swords and shields, accompanied by vigorous movements.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk/tribal dances of Arunachal Pradesh include Ponung, Aji Lamu, Chalo and Wancho.

• The Adi tribe celebrates festivals like Solung and Mopin.

• Arunachal Pradesh is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun' / 'Land of the Dawn-lit Mountains'.

NOTE

• Goa (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Dekhni, Fugdi and Dhalo.

• Odisha (Option 2): Known for the classical Odissi dance and folk dances like Ghumura.

• Jharkhand (Option 3): Known for tribal dances like Chhau, Paika and Jhumar.

question: In the eighteenth century, where did the Sikh community gather during Baisakhi and Diwali to take collective decisions called Gurmatas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amritsar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the eighteenth century, the Sikh community gathered at the Akal Takht in Amritsar (अमृतसर) during Baisakhi and Diwali to take collective decisions known as Gurmatas (गुरमता).

• A Gurmata was a resolution passed by the Sarbat Khalsa (the general assembly of the Sikhs).

• These gatherings helped the Sikhs coordinate political and military strategy.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Akal Takht ('Throne of the Timeless One') was established by Guru Hargobind in 1606.

• Amritsar houses the Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib), founded by Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan Dev.

• The Sikh misls (confederacies) organised themselves through these assemblies.

NOTE

• Nagpur (Option 1): A city in Maharashtra, not linked with Sikh Gurmata gatherings.

• Patna Sahib (Option 3): The birthplace of Guru Gobind Singh (a Takht), but not the venue of these gatherings.

• Bhopal (Option 4): The capital of Madhya Pradesh, unrelated to Sikh assemblies.

question: Which of the following bill provides details on the imposition, abolition, or regulation of taxes proposed in the budget?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Finance bill.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A Finance Bill (वित्त विधेयक) contains provisions concerning the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of taxes proposed in the Budget.

• It gives legal effect to the government's taxation proposals for the financial year.

• It is introduced in the Lok Sabha after the presentation of the Union Budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Finance Bills are dealt with under Article 110 and Article 117 of the Constitution.

• A Money Bill (Article 110) is a special category certified by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha.

• The Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes to a Money Bill/Finance Bill; the Lok Sabha may accept or reject them.

NOTE

• Private member bill (Option 2): A bill introduced by a member who is not a minister.

• Constitution amendment bill (Option 3): A bill to amend the Constitution under Article 368.

• Ordinary bill (Option 4): A bill concerning any matter other than financial/money matters, needing agreement of both Houses.

question:
As per the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act-2003, the actual deficits may exceed the targets only on which of the following ground?
I. National security
II. National calamity
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 (वित्तीय उत्तरदायित्व और बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम), actual deficits may exceed the targets only on grounds of national security and national calamity (and other exceptional situations).

• Hence both statements I and II are correct.

• These 'escape clauses' allow the government to deviate from fiscal deficit targets in extraordinary circumstances.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The FRBM Act, 2003 aims to institutionalise fiscal discipline and reduce the fiscal deficit.

• It was reviewed by the N. K. Singh Committee (2017), which recommended a debt-to-GDP target.

• The escape clause also covers situations like a decline in real output growth or structural reforms with fiscal implications.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect — national calamity is also a valid ground.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect — national security is also a valid ground.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect — both are recognised grounds under the Act.

question: _____ in Bihar was the capital of Magadha for several years. Later the capital was shifted to Pataliputra
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajagriha.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajagriha (राजगृह), present-day Rajgir in Bihar, was the early capital of Magadha for several years.

• Later the capital was shifted to Pataliputra (modern Patna) under the rulers of Magadha.

• Rajagriha was the capital during the Haryanka dynasty (Bimbisara and Ajatashatru).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The First Buddhist Council was held at Rajagriha soon after the death of Gautama Buddha.

• Rajagriha is surrounded by hills and was a major religious centre for Buddhism and Jainism.

• Udayin, son of Ajatashatru, is credited with shifting the capital to Pataliputra.

NOTE

• Ujjain (Option 2): An ancient city of the Avanti Mahajanapada in present-day Madhya Pradesh.

• Vaishali (Option 3): Capital of the Vajji/Lichchhavi confederacy, one of the world's earliest republics.

• Taxila (Option 4): An ancient centre of learning in the Gandhara region (present-day Pakistan).

question:
Which Veda contains hymns mostly taken from the Rigveda, arranged for singing?
I. Samaveda
II. Yajurveda
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Samaveda (सामवेद) contains hymns that are mostly borrowed from the Rigveda, arranged and set to melody for singing/chanting.

• Hence only Statement I is correct; the Yajurveda deals with sacrificial rituals, not chanting of Rigvedic hymns.

• The Samaveda is regarded as the origin of Indian classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda and Atharvaveda.

• The Rigveda is the oldest Veda, containing hymns in praise of gods.

• The Yajurveda contains rituals and sacrificial formulae, while the Atharvaveda contains spells and charms.

NOTE

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect — the Yajurveda is about rituals, not chanted Rigvedic hymns.

• Both I and II (Option 3): Incorrect — only the Samaveda fits the description.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect — the Samaveda clearly matches the description.
